name: Berlin by Night: Kindred and Institutions of Note

text.content:
Ellison Humboldt is Berlin's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} elder and, in truth, the single most powerful individual in the divided city — more powerful than either prince realizes. Operating an information network built on the city's sewers and its new subway tunnels, Ellison sells accurate intelligence and carefully seeded disinformation to both Gustav Breidenstein and Wilhelm Waldburg alike, and has done so for so long that neither prince thinks to doubt him. He maintains a lavishly furnished haven hidden in ancient sewer lines beneath the Europa Center, protected by security guards Blood Bound to him personally, and is believed to keep a secondary bolt-hole beneath Bellevue Palace as well.

Ellison could end the cold war between East and West Berlin with a single well-placed word, but chooses not to: his clan's unusual freedom and prestige in Berlin depends entirely on the continued value of the information he provides, and a unified city under one prince would sharply diminish both. He organizes the local @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} information network on Ellison's own terms, extracting favors and leniency for that clan from both princes in exchange for what they bring him. His only true confidant is the Nosferatu elder Rasputin, whose subtle manipulations can turn Ellison from concealing information to announcing it. Unbeknownst to most of Berlin's Kindred, Ellison ultimately answers to Baba Yaga, the Nosferatu Methuselah, and gathers intelligence on her behalf as much as his own.

The infamous mystic and confidant of the Romanov court did not die in 1916 as history records; he was Embraced into Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} and now dwells among Berlin's undead, one of Ellison's few trusted allies. Rasputin delights in mocking visiting @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} with sarcastic well-wishes for "the great communist experiment," a habit that has earned him no favor from Gustav Breidenstein but that he seems entirely untroubled by. His genuine influence lies in his relationship with Ellison: through careful, patient manipulation, Rasputin can turn the Nosferatu elder from suppressing a piece of information to broadcasting it, making him one of the few Kindred in Berlin capable of quietly steering the city's most powerful information broker.

Embraced in 1969 by Dieter Kotlar after a shared history of far-right political activism, Erika Geiger is both Dieter's childe and his lover, and one of the Final Reich's true believers rather than one of its manipulated pawns. She and Dieter hunt together, targeting immigrants and foreigners with the same racist zeal that drew her to Dieter in the first place. She holds real influence over Dieter, though she generally chooses to exercise it quietly and sparingly rather than openly.

Peter Kleist serves as Wilhelm Waldburg's interpreter, liaison, and chief bodyguard, and by extension one of the most trusted and influential Kindred in West Berlin. He personally arranges hospitality for any visiting Kindred whom Wilhelm chooses to favor, escorting guests, granting requested favors, and introducing them to guides — a courtesy that conveniently lets Wilhelm keep a close watch on outside Kindred moving through his domain. Peter's personal history began generations back: his sire was Embraced against Wilhelm's Retainer, a woman Wilhelm loved and ultimately chose to spare rather than punish for violating the Masquerade, a mercy that bound Peter's family in loyalty to Wilhelm ever since. Fanatically protective of the prince, Peter never uses foul language for fear of embarrassing Wilhelm's guests, but nurses a hot temper underneath his polished manners — a temper that has cost him torpor more than once.

The Final Reich, also called the Fourth Reich, is Berlin's most visible anarch group and the city's only officially acknowledged source of organized anarch trouble — though it is far from the only real threat to the city's stability. To most Kindred it appears to be little more than a nuisance run by unruly Malkavians, but its true leadership belongs to Dieter Kotlar, a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} true believer in the Reich's Nazi ideology, and its true master is Heinrich Himmler, who secretly uses the group to expand @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} influence throughout Berlin and, eventually, all of Europe. The Reich has claimed credit for terrorist activity it did little to actually cause, inflating its reputation, but it has genuinely fueled a resurgence of Nazi activity and racist violence in the city. Its membership swells and shrinks unpredictably depending on the whims of whichever @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} currently holds the clan's weekly "elder of the week" lottery, since the Reich's ranks are padded or purged according to that individual's mood.

pages.name: The Straitjacket Dancing Club of West Berlin

text.content: What began as a prank by a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} named Ozty during one of his brief weeks as elder of Berlin's Malkavian clan has become one of West Berlin's most feared urban legends. Ozty ordered the entire Malkavian clan to tie-dye liberated straitjackets, paint their faces like mimes, and descend on Groppiusstadt's nightclubs for a night of chaos; the disguise proved so useful for concealing identity that both the anarch Hunting Party and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} have since adopted it for their own, far more violent purposes. Sightings of the Dancing Club now span the western half of the city, from harmless dancing revelers to bands bashing in skulls, sometimes reportedly on the same night in different neighborhoods. No one, not even the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}, is entirely certain how many Kindred belong to the Straitjacket Dancing Club at any given time; estimates range from five to thirty.

The traditional haven of Gustav Breidenstein, Prince of East Berlin, the Berlin Palace anchors Gustav's claim to be close to the heart of the entire city, not merely its eastern half. Gustav has declared several sites throughout the Mitte district as Elysium, including the Tierpark Zoo, the original Berlin Town Hall (a location of deep sentimental significance to Kindred and kine alike), St. Nicholas's Church, and the Pergamon Museum — all enforced zones of neutrality where violence and open displays of vampiric nature are strictly forbidden on pain of Final Death.

Wilhelm Waldburg's haven and seat of power in West Berlin, Charlottenburg Castle is a combined park, museum, and tourist attraction that was devastated by Allied bombing in November 1943 and painstakingly restored after the war. Wilhelm additionally enforces strict Elysium at West Berlin's museums — including the Berlin Film Museum and the Berlin National Art Gallery, kept open late for exactly this purpose — at the particular insistence of the city's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} elder, who spends much of her unlife in these galleries and personally enforces their neutrality.
